main_text.head: CONCIO IX. Genes. 24.
main_text.p: ORrò Abraham senuit, venitq; in dies: & Dominus benedixit Abraham in cunctis. Et dixit Abraham ad seruum suum, seniorem domus suæ: qui præerat omnibus, quæ illius erant: Pone (inquiens) manum tuam subter fœmur meum. Et adiurabo te per Dominum Deum cœli et Deum terræ, ut non accipias uxorem filio meo de filiabus Chanaan, in quorum medio ego habito. Sed ad terram meam & ad patriam meam ibis, & accipies uxorem filio meo Isaac. Dixit vero seruus ille ad eum: Fortasse renuet mulier illa venire post me ad terram istam, & nunquid reducendo reducere debeo filium tuum ad terram unde tu egressus es? Cui respondit Abraham: Caue ne forte reducas filium meum illuc. Dominus Deus cœli, qui tulit me de domo patris mei, & de terra natiuitatis meæ, & qui locutus est ad me, quique iurauit mihi, dicens, Semini tuo dabo terram istam, ipse mittet angelum suum ante te, & accipies,

page.notes: Woodcut initial "D" in a decorative frame, joined to "ORrò"? The printed first word is "Orrò" with the woodcut standing for the first letter; I have read it as the initial O of "ORrò" and written the first word as printed ("Orrò"). Text runs to the bottom of the page with no catchword. Some letters are in long-s style and are normalised to s per the rules (e.g. "senuit", "suæ"). "Abraham" and "Isaac" are set in italic in the scan; the "A" of Abraham is printed as a reversed-ligature form in places and is transcribed as Abraham. Last word of the page "pies," is printed on its own line at the right, transcribed as "accipies," with the printed "pies," carried over from the line before; the last line reads "pies," in print and is marked here as a continuation of "accipies". The top-left figure "8o" is the printed page number 80.
